title: Features and Distractors
outcome: By the end, I can test a distracting feature with controlled changes rather than confounding clues.
scenario: A fictional book-topic classifier sees mystery books with triangular logos and science books with circular logos.
given: Training contains no mystery-circle or science-triangle covers.
Goal is to identify topic from actual subject information, not publisher logo. New controlled test outputs have not been supplied.

steps.label: Spot confounding
steps.detail: Topic and logo always move together in the training set.

steps.label: Hold topic fixed
steps.detail: Compare the same mystery description with triangle versus circle logo.

steps.label: Hold logo fixed
steps.detail: Compare mystery versus science descriptions with identical triangle logo.

steps.label: Observe separately
steps.detail: Record predictions before concluding which clue the classifier uses.

explanation: Either subject information or logo could explain success on the old combinations. Controlled pairs separate their predictions by changing one aspect at a time. Designing the pair is not equivalent to observing the model’s response. Keep the descriptions identical when testing logo so differences do not have two possible causes.

counterfactual.change: The first controlled pair yields mystery for triangle and science for circle.
counterfactual.prediction: That pair is evidence of unwanted logo sensitivity.
counterfactual.reason: The subject description stayed mystery; only the irrelevant logo changed.

student_task: Does this one pair prove the classifier always ignores subject? Explain a narrower claim.
teacher_answer: No. It shows one topic-fixed prediction changed with logo in this case; additional balanced comparisons are needed to characterise behavior.
project_evidence: Test recommender features for shortcuts, keeping relevant subject information separate from superficial catalogue styling.
limits: Controlled observations support specific sensitivity claims; they do not reveal every internal feature a learned model uses.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.
